data.name: Bokhur
data.gender_notes: Bokhur is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Bokhur is derived from Persian, meaning 'wise' or 'intelligent'. This name carries a rich historical significance as it was the name of a renowned Persian scholar and philosopher, Al-Bokhari. The name Bokhur carries the meaning “Wise, Intelligent” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Bokhur usually hope their child will grow to embody wise, intelligent and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bokhur total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_urdu.name: بُخور
in_urdu.meaning: رائحہ انگیز مادہ، بخور، خوشبو دینے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: بُخور (bukhoor) کا نام عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے خوشبو یا رائحہ انگیز مادہ۔ اسلامی روایات میں بخور کا ذکر خاص اہمیت کا حامل ہے کیونکہ اسے جنت کی خوشبوؤں میں سے ایک کہا جاتا ہے۔

in_pashto.name: بخور
in_pashto.long_meaning: بخور (bokhor) دى يو ماده چې د سوزولو په وخت خوشبوي خپروي. په اسلامي رواياتو کې د بخور يادونه شوې ده او دا د جنت د خوشبويو څخه يو ګڼل کيږي.

historical_references.reference: Bokhur was an important city in the Islamic world during the Silk Road era. It was a major center of trade, learning, and culture, with a renowned university known as the Bokhara Madrasah.
historical_references.context: Bokhur was a significant stopping point on the Silk Road, attracting merchants, scholars, and travelers from various parts of the world. The city was ruled by various Islamic dynasties, including the Samanids, Karakhanids, and Timurids, and its intellectual and cultural achievements contributed to the flowering of the Islamic Golden Age.

historical_references.reference: During the Timurid Empire (1370-1507 CE), Bokhur was the capital city and a major center of Islamic art and architecture. Timur, the founder of the empire, made Bokhur his capital after his conquest of the region.
historical_references.context: Bokhur flourished under Timur and his successors, who patronized the arts and sciences, resulting in the creation of many architectural masterpieces and the development of a distinctive Timurid style in Islamic art. The city was a hub of cultural exchange and attracted scholars, artists, and craftsmen from all over the Islamic world.
